Grail Planner

The holy grail is finding every unique and set item at least once. How the filter shows the items you haven't found yet, how long the grail takes in T1-T3 maps, what makes it faster, which items will take the longest, and where to target farm each item.

    How the filter shows your grail

      How fast the grail fills

      Grail items found after a number of full map clears, counting only the items T1-T3 map monsters can drop: without a Corrupted Ear, with one of the seven ears (the band, from the best to the worst), and switching ears, which means using, on each map, the ear expected to find the most items you don't have yet.

      Your Grail

      Tick the items you have under Every Item, or fill in your grail at the end of this tab: tick everything but what you're missing, or paste a list. From your ticks and the bar's settings this is your plan: the Corrupted Ear to run, the items a kill finds faster than a map and where to farm them, what a unique map's boss finds, and the slowest ones. Each missing item gets its best bet. Your ticks are kept in this browser only.

        Every ear for your missing items

        The best ear depends on the goal: the most of your missing items in your next 100 maps, 90% of them, or all of them.

        Fill in your grail: tick everything, paste a list, copy your ticks
        • Found most of it? Type what you're missing in the box, one name per line, and press "Tick all but these": every other item gets ticked. In game, the stash's Uniques and Sets tabs list what you're missing when you turn on "Show Undiscovered" (hover an item for its name). Or press "Tick all" and untick them one by one under Every Item: type a name in its search and press Enter.
        • Found a few? Type them in the box and press "Tick these", or tick them under Every Item. For a whole set or base at once, search it there and press "Tick shown".
        • The box's buttons: "Tick these" adds the names to your ticks, "Untick these" takes them off, "Tick all but these" ticks every item but the names, and "Replace my ticks" ticks the names and unticks everything else.
        • What the box reads: one item per line, from a spreadsheet, another grail tracker or typed by hand (Harlequin Crest, Arm of King Leoric). Capitals, apostrophes, a leading "The", bullets, numbering and a ticked box such as [x] don't matter, a version in brackets counts as the item (Harlequin Crest (Shako)), and a spreadsheet row counts by the cell with the name. Lines with an empty box ([ ]) and rows marked no, false or ✗ are skipped, and the lines it doesn't recognise are listed under the buttons (the first 10). Items that don't count for the grail (How It's Worked Out names them) are listed apart.
        • Keep or move your ticks: "Copy" copies the list of your ticks ("Show my list" shows it in the box). On another browser or device, paste it into this box and press "Replace my ticks".
        • Undo takes back your changes one at a time, latest first, while you stay on the page.

        Reading the table

        No ear

        Any ear

        Best ear
        with the ear whose pool has the item's base (the next ears under it)
        Best ear ×
        how many times more often the best ear finds it
        Maps for 90%
        the maps for a 90% chance to see it, with its best ear
        Drop level

        Marking what you've found

        • Tick its box, or type its name in the search and press Enter, then the next name
        • Tick shown / Untick shown: every row the search and filters list (a whole set, a base, every set item)
        • Found most of the grail? Tick all under Fill in your grail, then untick what you're missing (Show: "Not ticked" and "Ticked" check your work)
        • Undo takes your changes back one at a time
        • Paging through the game's Compendium? Sort by Compendium order, or switch to the Compendium view

        Target Farming

        Maps find the most grail items over time. For an item maps rarely drop, killing one boss or superunique again and again can be the better bet. Here is every act boss, superunique and special encounter in each difficulty, and the three unique map bosses that drop random uniques, with the grail items each drops per kill (per run, vault, map or shop where it says so).

          Unique Map Bosses

          The bosses of four unique maps drop extra loot when they die, on top of their own: three drop random uniques, Djinn's Domain's two Djinns a treasure explosion each. Each run takes a map: here is what one finds, against a whole T1-T3 map.

            Lucion Chests

            Lucion's chests drop better loot than any monster: their equipment comes out unique, set or rare far more often. They stand in Lucion's vault and in the Bitter Depths map event. Here is what they find, against a whole T1-T3 map.

              Gambling

              Gambling buys an unidentified item of a base you pick, for gold. Each one has a 1 in 2,000 chance to be unique and 1 in 1,000 to be a set item, whatever your magic find, and it counts for your grail like a drop. The table ranks the gamble bases by the gold they take per new grail item: for your missing items once you tick some, else for a fresh grail. Click a base for every item it can find, uniques and sets apart.

                Gheed's Map Event

                  Which offers to buy

                  Each base Gheed can show, how often a shop of 5 offers has it, the uniques it can be and the chance it is one you're missing (once you tick some; else any grail item), so the gold a new grail item costs if you buy it. An offer you'd rather skip costs nothing: the next shop's offers are new rolls.

                  What makes it faster

                    Maps for 90% of the map grail, without an ear and with the best single ear, at every setting.

                      What a Corrupted Ear does

                        Each ear

                        What each ear's pool adds. The count is the uniques and sets its pool can make; the list shows the items it raises most over a map without an ear, and how often each drops with that ear. "Show all" lists every grail item in the ear's pool.

                        Hard to find in maps

                        Never from map monsters

                        The slowest in maps

                        The items that take the most maps, even with the best ear, and their best farm spot. For most of them no ear's pool has the base, so only the extra drop helps. A farm spot counts kills, not maps: whether it beats maps depends on how fast you kill it and how fast you clear a map.

                        How this was worked out

                        • The grail: every unique and set item in the game, unique maps, quest items and nine uniques that don't count for the grail left out (Itherael's Path, Overlord's Helm, Dark Abyss, Aidan's Scar, Hadriel's Hand, Band of Skulls, Cage of the Unsullied, The Third Eye and Rainbow Facet). An item that comes in several versions (Akarat's Devotion, Cyclopean Roar and Arm of King Leoric twice) is one grail item: any of its versions finds it, so its chances are those of all its versions together.
                        • Spots: "fixed" means the monster stands in the same place every game: its area is one of the game's preset maps (the Cathedral, Tower Cellar Level 5, Nihlathak's Temple...), or laid out the same way every game (Travincal, the Chaos Sanctuary, the Bloody Foothills), or it waits in a piece the game always puts at the same edge of its area (Eldritch by the Bloody Foothills, Stormtree in the Flayer Jungle at its border with Lower Kurast). The others stand in a piece of the area the game places anywhere in it. "Areas from a waypoint" counts the areas to walk through from the nearest waypoint (towns have one; portals count as one step).
                        • Drops: each monster's drops and their quality as the game rolls them: each base's chance to be unique or set at the monster's level (class items have their own, better chances), magic find with its diminishing returns, and a unique picked among the base's uniques by their weight. A unique roll on a base with no unique becomes a rare, a set roll with no set item magic.
                        • Maps: full clears, averaged over the maps of a tier, from the map model behind the filter's experience tags (monsters per area, elite packs, monster levels). "Rare" is the average rare map with a corruption. Solo; one map boss per map, each map's own: its own loot at its own level (80 to 91; map bosses keep their level as other bosses do).
                        • Grail progress: each item drops at random at its own rate, so the items found after n maps add up item by item. "Switching" works from the expected progress; with your real ticks the planner does better.
                        • Best bet: an item's best bet compares one kill with one map: target farming its best boss or superunique (any difficulty; Corrupted Zones, ubers, events and unique map bosses left out) when one kill there finds it at least as often as a whole map with the item's best ear, maps otherwise. That's as if a kill took as long as a map; a quicker kill makes farming better still. Your Grail's plan sorts your missing items by it, and splits the maps' ones by their chance in your next 100 maps with the ear it names: an even chance or better, or the slowest.
                        • Farm spots: one kill of each act boss and superunique in each difficulty, solo: the monster's own drop at its own level. The drops of the minions around a superunique are counted apart, as "with its minions". In Normal difficulty a monster has a fixed level of its own; in Nightmare and Hell it takes the area's level, but bosses keep theirs; superuniques and their minions are 3 levels higher. A kill makes at most six items, gold and potions included, so Duriel's many picks always end at six. A boss drops its quest loot only while the quest is open; farming kills drop the usual loot.
                        • Cow King's Leathers: only a Hell Bovine's drop can be one of its pieces: the cows of the Secret Cow Level and the Cow King. Blood Moon's cows are other monsters and never drop it. Maps have Hell Bovines two ways, and the page counts both for these three items: the Bovine guest ("Map contains Hell Bovines"), a prefix on about 1 rare T1 map in 18 and 1 T2 or T3 map in 28, which adds the cows to every area's monsters (in groups and elite packs, beside the map's own) with +25-30% density and +15-20% magic find; and the Dark Wanderer map event, whose three wanderers each turn into a random act boss or superunique: the Cow King, with his 8 Hell Bovines, in about 1 rare map in 260 and 1 non-magical map in 800 (if you meet all three). Map guests and events are left out for every other item, but for the Bitter Depths.
                        • The Bitter Depths: the map event in about 1 rare T1-T3 map in 26 and 1 non-magical map in 80 (its portal opens late in a clear: counted for 97% of full clears). Its 20 Lucion chests drop as tier-0 vault chests, 5 items each; its monsters (5 elite packs) and Zoltun Kulle drop as map monsters do, and your ear works on them, not on the chests. Zoltun's death also sets off a treasure explosion: his loot again and again until 60 items lie on the ground, at his level, with no magic find (your ear doesn't touch it either). Its 7 sparkly chests are left out (about 3% of its chests' grail drops). Every map's numbers include it at that chance.
                        • Corrupted Zones: in Hell games made with Baal's quest done, one group of areas at a time has area level 85, so its superuniques are level 88 (bosses keep their own level).
                        • Unique map bosses: three unique maps' bosses drop random uniques when they die, on top of their own loot: Gregus Mazi in City of Ureh 3 (socketed), Warlord of Blood 2 or 3 (corrupted) and Na-Krul in Na-Krul's Abyss 3 (ethereal, but for the indestructible ones). Each one starts as a unique of the game picked at random, every unique alike but the few that never drop (Rainbow Facets are in; Gregus Mazi passes over bases that take no sockets). Na-Krul drops the unique he picked. Warlord of Blood and Gregus Mazi keep only its base and make a unique of it at item level 99, picked as any dropped unique is, by how common each unique of that base is (one already dropped in the game comes out rare). Their own loot drops as a map boss's does, at their level (91), with the map's own magic find. Djinn's Domain's two Djinns, Siren of the Forgotten Vault and Djinn of a Thousand Blades, each set off a treasure explosion when they die: their own loot again and again until 60 items lie on the ground, at their level (90), with no magic find; their own loot drops too, a second time half the time (the map's extra drop). Unique maps open only in Hell, one a game; their minibosses (Zayl the Merciful, Cory the Imp, Onion the Accused) drop only their own loot. One run a map; the rest of the map isn't counted.
                        • Ubers and events: Lilith, Uber Duriel and Uber Izual drop their own loot at level 110. Diablo Clone drops Annihilus every kill; Uber Tristram drops the Hellfire Torch once a run, when its last boss dies (the three bosses drop nothing else). The Uber Ancients: before touching the altar you switch on the ancients you want to fight at their statues, one, two or all three; the altar then drops 20 to 29 items for one ancient, 32 to 47 for two and 44 to 65 for three, at item level 90. Lucion's vault has 10 chests at every tier (0, 1 and 2, easiest first); each drops up to 3 items, then 2, 3 or 4 more from better loot on tier 0, 1 or 2, so a harder tier gives more items, not better ones. The items have the vault's level; the level of the character who opens the chest (95 here) goes into their quality. The numbers are for the whole vault; Lucion himself drops no grail items. The vault's key is cubed from three parts, each a chance per kill in Hell (Lucion Chests names them; solo, as every number here).
                        • Gheed's map event: each of his 5 offers is a random unique: any unique but jewels and the few that never drop. One that needs character level 60 or more is turned down (level − 49)% of the time and another picked; in one shop in 200, one offer is a special ring instead.
                        • Gambling: each gambled item's item level is your character level −5 to +4. The base becomes exceptional with a chance that grows 0.9% per item level above the exceptional version's level, else elite with 0.33% per level above the elite version's (only once the exceptional chance is above zero). Then it is unique 1 time in 2,000 and a set item 1 time in 1,000, picked among the uniques or sets of that base whose level is at most the item level, like a drop; with none, the roll is lost. Magic find plays no part. The gold: rings 50,000, amulets 63,000; any other base costs more the higher your character level, and the more so the higher its exceptional and elite versions' prices (no reduced vendor prices here).
                        • Left out: T4 dungeons, unique maps and whole area clears: a full Cow Level, Chaos Sanctuary or Baal run also drops from every monster on the way, so those runs find more than the boss alone shows here. PD2's special drops (sigils, Corrupted Zone shards) aren't grail items.
